items.title: The Mahāyāna's Own Blind Spot: Emptiness Badly Misread

items.zh: 復何因緣，或有起如是見，立如是論：無有一切諸法體相？答：以於如來所說甚深經中，相似甚深離言說法不能如實正覺了故。又於安立法相不如正理而思惟故，起於空見。彼作是念：決定無有諸法體相。
items.en: By what further cause do some arrive at this view and establish this doctrine — that no phenomenon whatsoever has any real characteristic at all? Because they fail to genuinely, correctly awaken to what the Tathāgata actually meant in his profound scriptures by the verbal teachings that are the likeness of the profound truth beyond all verbal expression — and because they fail to reflect soundly on how phenomena's characteristics are conventionally established, they give rise to this empty view. They come to think: phenomena definitely have no real characteristic at all.

items.title: The Refutation: Karma Can Ripen Late, Parents Are Still Parents, and the Intermediate State Simply Escapes Ordinary Sight

items.zh: 今應問彼：汝何所欲？為有生所受業及後所受業，為一切皆是生所受耶？若俱有者，汝先所說無有施與，無有愛養，無有祠祀，無有妙行，無有惡行，無有妙行、惡行業果異熟，無此世間，無彼世間，不應道理。若言無有後所受者，諸有造作淨與不淨種種行業，彼命終已，於彼生時，頓受一切淨與不淨業果異熟，不應道理。
items.en: One should press them: what do you actually intend — is there karma that ripens in the very next life, as well as karma that ripens only in some later life, or does all karma ripen in the very next life alone? If both kinds exist, then your earlier claim that there is no giving, and so on, makes no sense, since your clairvoyance saw only a single, immediately following life. If only next-life karma exists, then anyone who performed a mixture of wholesome and unwholesome deeds should, in their very next life, experience every one of those results all at once — which plainly does not happen, and makes no sense either.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？凡從彼胎藏及從彼種子而生者，彼等於此為是父母？為非父母耶？若言是父母者，汝言無父無母，不應道理。若言彼非父母者，從彼胎藏及彼種子所生，而言非父非母，不應道理。若時為父母，是時非男女；若時為男女，是時非父母；無不定過。
items.en: Further, what do you actually intend: are those from whose womb and seed a person is born their true parents, or not? If they are, then your claim of no parents makes no sense. If they are not, then denying that the very source of one's own womb and seed counts as one's parent makes no sense either. Note there is no real inconsistency here: at the time one is a parent, one is not simultaneously a child; at the time one is a child, one is not simultaneously a parent — a role reversing across different lifetimes creates no logical contradiction at all.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？為有彼處受生眾生，天眼不見？為無有耶？若言有者，汝言無有化生眾生，不應道理。若言無者，是則撥無離想欲者、離色欲者、離三界欲者，不應道理。
items.en: Further, what do you actually intend: are there places of rebirth genuinely invisible even to the divine eye, or not? If there are, then your claim that no spontaneously born beings exist makes no sense — it simply escaped your sight. If there are not, then denying the plainly real existence of those free of desire for perception, free of desire for form, or free of desire for all three realms makes no sense either.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？為有阿羅漢性，而於彼起增上慢？為無有耶？若言有者，汝言世間必定無有真阿羅漢，不應道理。若言無者，若有發起不正思惟，顛倒自謂是阿羅漢，此乃應是真阿羅漢，亦不中理。
items.en: Further, what do you actually intend: does a genuine state of arhatship exist, of which someone may hold an inflated, mistaken conceit — or does no such state exist at all? If it exists, then your claim that there is definitely no genuine arhat in the world makes no sense, since a counterfeit presupposes a genuine original. If it does not exist, then the very person who mistakenly, deludedly believed themselves an arhat would, by your own logic, have to actually be one — which is equally absurd.

items.title: The Three Natures Cannot All Be Denied, and Doctrine Thirteen Closes

items.zh: 又應問彼：汝何所欲？圓成實相法、依他起相法、遍計所執相法為有？為無？若言有者，汝言無有一切諸法體相，不應道理。若言無者，應無顛倒，亦無染淨，不應道理。
items.en: One should further press the Mahāyāna misreader: what do you actually intend — do the perfected nature, the dependent nature, and the imagined nature exist, or not? If they exist, then your claim that no phenomenon whatsoever has any real characteristic makes no sense. If none of them exists, then there should be no such thing as distorted misperception at all, nor any such thing as defilement or purity — which plainly does not accord with how things actually are.

items.zh: 如是若生後所受故，非不決定故，有生處故，有增上慢故，有三種相故，不應道理。是故此論非如理說。
items.en: Thus, because of what is experienced after birth, because it is not undetermined, because there are places of birth, because there is overestimation, and because there are three kinds of characteristic, it does not accord with reason. Therefore this doctrine is not soundly reasoned.

items.title: The Fourteenth Doctrine: One Caste Born From the Creator's Own Mouth

items.zh: 妄計最勝論者，謂如有一，若沙門、若婆羅門，起如是見，立如是論：婆羅門是最勝種類，剎帝利等是下劣種類；婆羅門是白淨色類，餘種是黑穢色類；婆羅門種可得清淨，非餘種類；諸婆羅門是梵王子，從大梵王口腹所生，從梵所出，梵所變化，梵王體胤。
items.en: The doctrine of false supremacy: there are certain renunciants or brahmins who hold such a view and establish such a doctrine — that brahmins are the supreme caste and warriors and the rest are inferior castes; that brahmins are of a pure, fair complexion while the other castes are of a dark, impure complexion; that only the brahmin caste can attain purity, and no other; and that brahmins alone are the sons of the great Brahmā, born directly from his mouth and belly, issuing from him, transformed by him, his own bodily lineage.

items.zh: 謂鬪諍劫諸婆羅門作如是計。問：何因緣故，諸婆羅門起如是見，立如是論？答：由教及理故。教如前說。理者，謂如有一，為性尋思，乃至廣說。
items.en: This is what the brahmins of the age of strife hold. Question: For what reason do those brahmins hold this view and establish this doctrine? Answer: Because of scripture and reasoning. Scripture is as explained before. Reasoning means that someone is a speculator by nature, and so on at length.

items.title: Why This Claim Took Hold, and the Refutation: Every Caste Shares the Same Birth, Karma, and Livelihood

items.zh: 以見世間真婆羅門性具戒故，有貪名利及恭敬故，作如是計。今應問彼：汝何所欲？為唯餘種類從父母產生？為婆羅門亦爾耶？若唯餘種類者，世間現見諸婆羅門從母產生，汝謗現事，不應道理。若婆羅門亦爾者，汝先所說諸婆羅門是最勝種類，剎帝利等是下種類，不應道理。
items.en: This claim arose from observing that a genuinely virtuous brahmin, one who upholds precepts, exists in the world, while members of other castes are seen craving wealth, reputation, and honour. One should press them: what do you actually intend — are only the other castes born from parents, or are brahmins born the very same way? If only the other castes, then this plainly contradicts what everyone can see: brahmins are plainly born from their mothers too — denying plain fact makes no sense. If brahmins are born the very same way, then your claim that brahmins are a supreme caste while warriors and the rest are inferior makes no sense at all.

items.zh: 如從母產生，如是造不善業，造作善業，造身語意惡行，造身語意妙行，於現法中受愛不愛果，便於後世生諸惡趣，或生善趣。若三處現前，是彼是此，由彼由此，入於母胎，從之而生。若世間工巧處，若作業處。
items.en: Just as with being born from a mother, so too with performing unwholesome or wholesome karma, with bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct or good conduct, with experiencing desirable or undesirable results in this present life, and with being reborn afterwards into an unfortunate or a fortunate destiny; so too with the three conditions being present for conception — as this one or that one, through that one or this one — entering the mother's womb, and being born from it; and so too with every worldly craft and every ordinary occupation.

blocks.text: Today contains one of the most important passages in the treatise for understanding Yogācāra's relation to Madhyamaka. The second part of the empty view is held, the treatise says, by followers of the Mahāyāna who misread the teaching of emptiness. Yogācāra's answer is the **three natures**, which you met in Introduction 1. Then the fourteenth doctrine begins: that one caste is superior by birth.

Missing from Ru-Yi's translation, now supplied in our own: 0311c19–c22 (a summary of why the empty view fails) and 0311c28–0312a03 ("it is the brahmins of the age of strife who hold this"; why they hold it).

The second claim of the empty view, "no phenomenon has any real characteristic", comes from those who "fail to awaken to what the Tathāgata meant in his profound scriptures by teachings that resemble the profound truth beyond words, and reflect unsoundly on how phenomena's characteristics are established". Both teachers identify them as students of Madhyamaka who went astray. Venerable Miào Jìng: "not in line with Nāgārjuna". This is the classical Yogācāra charge of **wrongly grasped emptiness** (惡取空).
Master Cháng Bǎi: the sūtras have two profundities, emptiness and dependent origination. The wrong-graspers keep only the first: "everything is false; that is the true meaning."

Venerable Miào Jìng explains "teachings that resemble" (相似) without any negative sense: the Buddha's spoken teaching can only resemble the realised truth, which is beyond words. Mistaking the resemblance for the thing, one concludes that since words fail, nothing is there.

The first part of the empty view is answered first. Karma may ripen in the next life or later; if only next-life karma existed, someone who did mixed deeds would have to receive every result at once. Roles change between lives: whoever is your parent now is not your child now, so the shifting of roles across lives is no contradiction. And the false depends on the real. Master Cháng Bǎi: "there must be true arhats for there to be false ones."

subs.head: The three natures cannot all be denied

blocks.text: Then the decisive question to the Mahāyāna nihilist: "Do the perfected nature, the dependent nature, and the imagined nature exist, or not? If they exist, your claim that no phenomenon has any characteristic makes no sense. If not, there could be no distortion, defilement, or purity."

Venerable Miào Jìng matches them: **distortion** belongs to the imagined nature, **defilement** to the dependent nature, **purity** to the perfected nature. Master Cháng Bǎi's image: in a dream, the dream-objects are imagined; the dreaming mind is dependent, really present to produce the dream; waking, where neither dream nor dreaming mind is found, is like the perfected.

This is the heart of the Yogācāra position. Emptiness is true of the imagined nature: what we project does not exist. But the dependent nature, the process of experience, exists conventionally, and the perfected nature, its true character, is real. Deny all three and there is nothing to be deluded, nothing to purify, and no path.

The fourteenth doctrine: brahmins are the supreme caste, pure and fair, "sons of Brahmā born from his mouth". Master Cháng Bǎi recounts the myth: from Brahmā's mouth came brahmins, from his arms warriors, from his thighs merchants, from his feet labourers. Venerable Miào Jìng: "brahmin" means "pure conduct", and the age of strife is when clinging to "I" and "mine" is so strong that people always belittle others to raise themselves. The refutation, begun today and finished tomorrow, is that all castes are born, act, and attain in the same ways.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, why do some arrive at the view that no phenomenon has any real characteristic?
options: failing to awaken to the profound teachings that resemble the inexpressible, and reflecting unsoundly on how phenomena's characteristics are established
quiz.why: "Because they fail to genuinely, correctly awaken to what the Tathāgata actually meant in his profound scriptures by teachings that merely resemble a profound truth beyond all verbal expression — and because they fail to reflect soundly on how phenomena's characteristics are conventionally established." This error is internal to Buddhism.

quiz.q: Who, according to the teachers, are these "wrong-graspers of emptiness"?
options: students of Madhyamaka who learned it wrong — not in line with Nāgārjuna
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "These are students of Madhyamaka who've gone astray — not in line with Nāgārjuna." Master Cháng Bǎi: "rebuking those who learned Madhyamaka wrongly"; the right view is "existence is emptiness and emptiness existence — conditioned existence is precisely lack of own-nature."

quiz.q: What "two kinds of profundity" does Master Cháng Bǎi say the sūtras have, and where do the wrong-graspers go astray?
options: the profundity of emptiness and of dependent origination — they keep only "everything is false; that is the true meaning"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The Buddha's sūtras have two profundities: emptiness and dependent origination"; the wrong-graspers say "everything is false — that is the true meaning, and seeing so is right view," seeing emptiness but not dependent origination.

quiz.q: The first dilemma asks whether there is karma ripening next life and karma ripening later. If only next-life karma exists, what follows?
options: one who did mixed deeds would have to receive every result at once in the next life — absurd
quiz.why: "If only next-life karma exists, then anyone who performed a mixture of wholesome and unwholesome deeds should, in their very next life, experience every one of those results all at once." Master Cháng Bǎi: then would they go to heaven or hell? Venerable Miào Jìng: the outsiders saw next-life results but not later ones.

quiz.q: The text asks whether true arhatship exists, of which someone may be conceited. What principle do the teachers draw?
options: the counterfeit depends on the genuine — fake arhats prove real ones exist
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The false depends on the real — there must be true arhats for there to be false ones." Venerable Miào Jìng: "That there are fakes shows there are genuine ones." If no true arhat existed, the self-deluded one would have to be real — even more absurd.

quiz.q: How does the treatise refute the Mahāyāna wrong-graspers of emptiness?
options: do the perfected, dependent, and imagined natures exist? If so, "no characteristics" fails; if not, there could be no distortion, defilement, or purity
quiz.why: "Do the perfected nature, the dependent nature, and the imagined nature exist, or not? If they exist, then your claim that no phenomenon whatsoever has any real characteristic makes no sense. If none of them exists, then there should be no such thing as distorted misperception at all, nor any such thing as defilement or purity." Master Cháng Bǎi: wrong grasping of emptiness "slanders all three natures as nonexistent."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what does the doctrine of false supremacy claim?
options: brahmins are supreme, fair, alone able to attain purity, sons of Brahmā born from his mouth and belly
quiz.why: "Brahmins are the supreme caste … of a pure, fair complexion while the other castes are of a dark, impure complexion; … only the brahmin caste can attain purity … sons of the great Brahmā, born directly from his mouth and belly." B is the Buddha's own position — Master Cháng Bǎi: "The Blessed One taught the equality of the four castes."
